- **Items:** 7, each opened by the same refrain ("the next thing that screams old lady is"). Shortest: item 7, hair (83 words, 34 seconds); longest: item 6, untucked tops (152 words, 1:19). Typical 115 to 130 words, about a minute. Item one starts at 0:13, after 29 words (3% of the video): no intro at all. The order runs from the whole silhouette (baggy) to neckline, colour, shoes, prints, tucking, and ends on hair.
- **Item shape:** a fixed four-beat frame: the look (the refrain plus the item), the why (erases the silhouette, shortens the neck, makes you vanish, reads 80s), then "So, what can you do instead?" and the swap, then a one-line "My pro tip is" as the result. Item 7 has no pro tip. Checks are rare (no clogs and socks; a few inches off).
- **The title's promise:** "7 Things" (0:02; paid, counted by refrain, not by number); "Scream 'Old Lady'" (10 times, the refrain); "Harsh But True" (paid by the "tough love" opening and the 3:44 aside); "Style Over 50" (never said; the speech says "women over 60" at 1:47 and "our 70s" at 4:17).
- **Feelings:** 4 of 7 items name an inner feeling: item 1 (lost self-confidence, before; confidence, after), item 2 (open up your self-confidence, after), item 3 (invisible, before), item 6 (shows your tummy, before; younger and slimmer, after). Mostly said about "women" or "you".
- **Villain:** the garments; other women "hiding behind tons of fabric" (0:27); the past (stuck in the 80s, an old aunt's curtains). Mostly aimed at items, but the confidence line at 0:41 lands on the woman.
- **Hard words:** "old lady" 10 times (refrain, title-led), "aging" 4 (3:32, 6:41, 7:21, 7:23), "oldfashioned" and "uptight" (1:59, 2:02), "hobbit feet" (4:53), "love handles" (6:36). Flagged once as harsh on clothes, not on you (3:44).
- **CTA placement:** none spoken except the end-screen pointer at 7:51 (30 words). No subscribe, no product, no sponsor.
- **Ending:** a short goodbye and a pointer to the next video on screen. No recap.
- **What sets it apart from other models of its type:**
  - It is the shortest and tightest model: 923 words, no intro, a fixed refrain and a fixed four-beat item frame, ending each item on a quotable "pro tip".
  - The harshness is announced up front and defended mid-video ("harsh on your clothes, not on you"), so the hard word is a promise rather than a slip; comments still reject the word "old".
  - The French lens is used once, lightly, as a first-person observation; the rest is universal advice.
  - **How she frames French women (for Diane's lens):** one claim, said as "we" and unhedged: [4:14] "Here in France, we women even in our 70s and over, wear lovely shoes." It is an observation from inside, not a rule for all French women, and it is tied to a practical point (flat or low heel, never clumpy). No claim about Americans. Diane should keep the inside view but add a hedge ("many women here", "in Paris you'll see").

## Why it works

It promises hard truth and delivers it in eight minutes with no intro, a refrain viewers remember and a swap for every verdict. Humour softens it ("disappear faster than a macaron", an aunt's curtains), and the head-on-model images amuse: "the images of your head transposed on models wearing questionable outfits never fails to crack me up" (139 likes). The comments push back hard on the frame and two rules: "Hey, I'm dressed. Everyone should be thankful for that." (415 likes); "Waiting for the day when being old isn't an insult." (390 likes); "I disagree with tucking in blouses." (1.1K likes, the top viewer comment); "I think the opposite. All the sweet little old ladies at my church have short hair." (654 likes); "I no longer have a waistline. Am I alone?" (798 likes). Some agree and adapt: "I agree with everything except the tucking." (324 likes).

## Lines worth studying ([real] files only)

- Hook: [0:00] "Are you ready for little tough love? Today I'm revealing seven things that instantly scream old lady."
- The why: [0:41] "The truth is baggy clothes erase your silhouette and add years"
- The turn: [0:58] "follow your natural lines. Remember fitted does not mean tight. It means tailored to you."
- A feeling line: [2:42] "Yes, neutrals are classic, but beige on beige on beige, you disappear faster than a macaron at a Parisian cafe."
- The swap: [3:01] "instead? Add contrast to your face."
- The flagged hard word: [3:44] "I told you I was going to be harsh. Not on you, but your clothes. Cruel to be kind and all that."
- Permission: [4:04] "Comfort is non-negotiable. I agree with you. You don't have to suffer to be stylish."
- The French lens (an inside observation): [4:14] "Here in France, we women even in our 70s and over, wear lovely shoes."

## Doesn't transfer

- Lost confidence pinned on the woman: [0:41] "The truth is baggy clothes erase your silhouette and add years and hide what little self-confidence they may have left." (SHAMING, banned: keep the why on the garment).
- "Old lady" as the refrain: [0:02] "Today I'm revealing seven things that instantly scream old lady." Ten uses drew the strongest pushback in the comments ("Waiting for the day when being old isn't an insult.", 390 likes). Our scripts can name the fear once, then talk about the garment.
- Her own outfit and hair as proof: [3:21] "For instance, I am wearing a black penetr." and [7:27] "I can hear you say well Marian is want to talk with her short hair." (TRY-ON, banned).
- A reference to her own earlier video: [7:31] "not familiar with my hair problem. I addressed this in a previous video."
- Sign-off and end-screen pointer: [7:59] "that make you look older, watch the video on screen" (SIGN-OFF, banned).
- Mocking words for comfort shoes: [4:49] "looking. Say no to gladiator sandals or hobbit feet styles." (comments from women with wide or arthritic feet push back; give the comfortable swap without the jibe).
- Unhedged generalisation: [4:14] "Here in France, we women even in our 70s and over, wear lovely shoes." Diane may say this kind of thing only hedged ("many women here"), and never as a fact about all French women.
- Rules the audience rejects as universal (check against the brief): tucking [6:46] "can you do instead? Well, just tuck the front of your top inside the waistband" and short hair [7:41] "and so should our hairstyle. Usually a shorter cut, just a few inches off, is all you need." Both need an option for a larger middle or longer hair.
